## Answer: **1963**

The **People's Vanguard Party** (Arabic: حزب الطليعة الشعبية) was a political party in Yemen with its **headquarters in Aden, South Yemen**.

The major insurgency that began in this area was the **Aden Emergency** (also known as the Aden Insurgency), which started on **October 14, 1963**. This was an armed rebellion led mainly by the National Liberation Front (NLF) and the Front for the Liberation of Occupied South Yemen (FLOSY) against British colonial rule in South Arabia.

Key facts about the Aden Emergency:
- **Started:** October 14, 1963 (when tribes from Radfan attacked British troops)
- **Ended:** November 30, 1967
- **Result:** British withdrawal and independence of the People's Republic of Southern Yemen

There were later conflicts in the same region as well, including:
- Al-Qaeda insurgency in South Yemen (started 1998)
- Separatist Southern Movement insurgency (started April 27, 2009)

However, the **Aden Emergency of 1963** is the most historically significant insurgency associated with Aden, where the People's Vanguard Party maintained its headquarters.

# People's Vanguard Party (Yemen)
The **People's Vanguard Party** (Arabic: حزب الطليعة الشعبية), also referred to as **at-Tali'a**,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-1) was a [Ba'athist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ba'athism "Ba'athism") political party in Yemen.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-ta-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-3) The party was established in the late 1950s.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) It was the Yemeni branch of the Baath Party. When the Baath Party was divided between Syrian and Iraqi factions, the Yemeni branch overwhelmingly sided with the Syrian-led Ba'ath Party.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-hidi-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-6) After the split, the Syrian-aligned Ba'athists 'Yemenized' their party and took the name People's Vanguard Party.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-hidi-5)
[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Conference_of_the_People's_Vanguard,_South_Yemen.jpg)
The Third Conference of the People's Vanguard Party

# People's Vanguard Party (Yemen)
The members of the party were largely recruited from teachers, students, and intellectuals.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) The party was based in Aden, and had limited presence outside the city.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) It had some presence in Hadhramaut for a brief period.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) The party was banned in North Yemen, where it was part of the National Democratic Front and took part in the NDF Rebellion.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-hidi-5)
The party was one of two non-National Front (NF) parties tolerated during the early 1970s. In October 1975 it joined the NF-dominated United Political Organization of the National Front[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-Hobday-7) (which evolved into the Yemeni Socialist Party in 1978).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-ta-2) The merger was ratified by the third PVP congress held in August 1975.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-8)

The _Vanguardia Popular_ (People's Vanguard Party) is a communist political party in Costa Rica, originally founded in 1931 as the Communist Party of Costa Rica. This party flag has been in use since its establishment, representing its ideological alignment with international communism throughout its history, including its role in the 1948 Costa Rican Civil War. The design consists of a solid red field, symbolizing revolution and the working class, with a yellow torch, referencing Juan Santamaria who in Costa Rican history, prevented the Nicaraguan Fillibusters from taking over the nation. This flag is specific to the Costa Rican political party and should **not be confused with** the national flag of the Soviet Union or the flags of other national communist parties, which often feature yellow emblems or additional symbols.

# People's Vanguard Party (Yemen)
The **People's Vanguard Party** (Arabic: حزب الطليعة الشعبية), also referred to as **at-Tali'a**,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-1) was a [Ba'athist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ba'athism "Ba'athism") political party in Yemen.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-ta-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-3) The party was established in the late 1950s.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) It was the Yemeni branch of the Baath Party. When the Baath Party was divided between Syrian and Iraqi factions, the Yemeni branch overwhelmingly sided with the Syrian-led Ba'ath Party.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-hidi-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-6) After the split, the Syrian-aligned Ba'athists 'Yemenized' their party and took the name People's Vanguard Party.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-hidi-5)
[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Conference_of_the_People's_Vanguard,_South_Yemen.jpg)
The Third Conference of the People's Vanguard Party

# People's Vanguard Party (Yemen)
The members of the party were largely recruited from teachers, students, and intellectuals.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) The party was based in Aden, and had limited presence outside the city.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) It had some presence in Hadhramaut for a brief period.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) The party was banned in North Yemen, where it was part of the National Democratic Front and took part in the NDF Rebellion.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-hidi-5)
The party was one of two non-National Front (NF) parties tolerated during the early 1970s. In October 1975 it joined the NF-dominated United Political Organization of the National Front[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-Hobday-7) (which evolved into the Yemeni Socialist Party in 1978).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-ta-2) The merger was ratified by the third PVP congress held in August 1975.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-8)

The _Vanguardia Popular_ (People's Vanguard Party) is a communist political party in Costa Rica, originally founded in 1931 as the Communist Party of Costa Rica. This party flag has been in use since its establishment, representing its ideological alignment with international communism throughout its history, including its role in the 1948 Costa Rican Civil War. The design consists of a solid red field, symbolizing revolution and the working class, with a yellow torch, referencing Juan Santamaria who in Costa Rican history, prevented the Nicaraguan Fillibusters from taking over the nation. This flag is specific to the Costa Rican political party and should **not be confused with** the national flag of the Soviet Union or the flags of other national communist parties, which often feature yellow emblems or additional symbols.

# People's Vanguard Party (Yemen)
The **People's Vanguard Party** (Arabic: حزب الطليعة الشعبية), also referred to as **at-Tali'a**,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-1) was a [Ba'athist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ba'athism "Ba'athism") political party in Yemen.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-ta-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-3) The party was established in the late 1950s.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) It was the Yemeni branch of the Baath Party. When the Baath Party was divided between Syrian and Iraqi factions, the Yemeni branch overwhelmingly sided with the Syrian-led Ba'ath Party.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-hidi-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-6) After the split, the Syrian-aligned Ba'athists 'Yemenized' their party and took the name People's Vanguard Party.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-hidi-5)

# People's Vanguard Party (Yemen)
The members of the party were largely recruited from teachers, students, and intellectuals.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) The party was based in Aden, and had limited presence outside the city.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) It had some presence in Hadhramaut for a brief period.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-nbr-4) The party was banned in North Yemen, where it was part of the National Democratic Front and took part in the NDF Rebellion.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-hidi-5)
The party was one of two non-National Front (NF) parties tolerated during the early 1970s. In October 1975 it joined the NF-dominated United Political Organization of the National Front[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-Hobday-7) (which evolved into the Yemeni Socialist Party in 1978).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-ta-2) The merger was ratified by the third PVP congress held in August 1975.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Vanguard_Party_(Yemen)#cite_note-8)

The _Vanguardia Popular_ (People's Vanguard Party) is a communist political party in Costa Rica, originally founded in 1931 as the Communist Party of Costa Rica. This party flag has been in use since its establishment, representing its ideological alignment with international communism throughout its history, including its role in the 1948 Costa Rican Civil War. The design consists of a solid red field, symbolizing revolution and the working class, with a yellow torch, referencing Juan Santamaria who in Costa Rican history, prevented the Nicaraguan Fillibusters from taking over the nation. This flag is specific to the Costa Rican political party and should **not be confused with** the national flag of the Soviet Union or the flags of other national communist parties, which often feature yellow emblems or additional symbols.

The **Aden Emergency**, also known as the **14 October Revolution**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-8) or the **Aden Insurgency**, was an armed rebellion led mainly by the National Liberation Front (NLF) and the Front for the Liberation of Occupied South Yemen (FLOSY) against the British Protectorate and Federation of South Arabia. It began on 14 October 1963 when tribes from Radfan attacked British troops and ended with the proclamation of independence of the [People's Republic of Southern Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_Southern_Yemen "People's Republic of Southern Yemen").

The British had declared a state of emergency following the throwing of a grenade at a gathering of British officials on 10 December 1963 at RAF Khormaksar. A state of emergency was then declared in the British Crown colony of Aden and its hinterland, the Aden Protectorate. The emergency escalated in 1967, which hastened the end of British rule in the territory, which had begun in 1839.

### British arrival in Yemen
[edit]
The first political intercourse between Yemen and the British took place in 1799 during the French invasion of Egypt and Syria, when a naval force was sent from Britain, with a detachment of troops from India, to occupy the island of Perim and prevent all communication of the French in Egypt with the Indian Ocean, by way of the Red Sea. Due to the lack of water supply, the barren and inhospitable island of Perim was found unsuitable for troops.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-10) The Sultan of Lahej, Ahmed bin Abdul Karim, then received the detachment for some time at Aden. He proposed to enter into an alliance and to grant Aden as a permanent station, but the offer was declined. A treaty was, however, concluded with the Sultan in 1802 by Admiral Home Popham, who was instructed to enter into political and commercial alliances with the Chiefs of the Arabian coast of the Red Sea.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-:0-11)

### British arrival in Yemen
By the early 1800s, the British were looking for a coaling station to fuel their steamships through their journey from the Suez Canal to the British Raj.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark201029-12) The British tried to negotiate with the Mahra Sultanate to buy the island of Socotra, located in the Arabian Sea, but the Sultan of Mahra refused and told the British naval officer who was tasked with the mission that the island was "the gift of the Almighty to the Mahris".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark201029-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBijl20144-13) In 1835, a year after the British had given up on Socotra, they had attempted to purchase the port city of Aden and its inlet from the Sultan of Lahej, Muhsin Bin Fadl, but they failed. In 1837, the _Duria Dawla_, an Indian ship flying the Union Jack, crashed near the east coast of Aden and was looted by local tribesmen. A year after the incident, in 1838, British officials arrived in Lahej and demanded 12,000 Maria Theresa thalers (MTT) as compensation for the losses. The sultan, unable to pay that sum of money, was forced to cede Aden to the British for a sum of 8,700 MTT a year.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark201031-14) On 19 January 1839, the British East India Company landed Royal Marines at Aden to retain full control of Aden and stop attacks by pirates against British shipping to India.

By : Jonathan Walker
Publisher : Pen & Sword Military , 2014
Synopsis :
About this title :
During the early 1960s the Cold War reached its climax. Britain's dwindling power in the Middle East was under siege from Arab nationalism, the Communist bloc and from American designs in the region.
Aden, with its strategic military base and old Protectorate buffer zone, was soon the main battleground.
The 1962 Egyptian-inspired coup in the neighbouring Kingdom of North Yemen further tightened the noose. So began a bitter and bloody insurgency war in South Arabia. British regular an special forces were soon pitted against growing and formidable insurgency forces, fighting both a war in the mountains and an urban conflict in the backstreets of Aden. Intelligence agencies vied for control of 'hearts and minds'.
The British launched a clandestine war in Yemen to keep their enemies at bay. But still the situation in Aden spiralled out of control, culminating in a bloody slaughter in 1967.

# ADEN OLD MEMORIES | Aden Insurgency : | Facebook
In that November, the British Army finally withdrew from South Arabia. Aden Insurgency is the extraordinary story of Britain's last colonial conflict. Using a wide range of recently released archive and eye-witness accounts, the author charts the collapse of the South Arabian state. Set against a background of ruthless political ambition, these events shaped the Yemen of today.

The **Aden Emergency**, also known as the **14 October Revolution**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-8) or the **Aden Insurgency**, was an armed rebellion led mainly by the National Liberation Front (NLF) and the Front for the Liberation of Occupied South Yemen (FLOSY) against the British Protectorate and Federation of South Arabia. It began on 14 October 1963 when tribes from Radfan attacked British troops and ended with the proclamation of independence of the [People's Republic of Southern Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_Southern_Yemen "People's Republic of Southern Yemen").
texts.2: The British had declared a state of emergency following the throwing of a grenade at a gathering of British officials on 10 December 1963 at RAF Khormaksar. A state of emergency was then declared in the British Crown colony of Aden and its hinterland, the Aden Protectorate. The emergency escalated in 1967, which hastened the end of British rule in the territory, which had begun in 1839.
texts.3:
### British arrival in Yemen
[edit]
The first political intercourse between Yemen and the British took place in 1799 during the French invasion of Egypt and Syria, when a naval force was sent from Britain, with a detachment of troops from India, to occupy the island of Perim and prevent all communication of the French in Egypt with the Indian Ocean, by way of the Red Sea. Due to the lack of water supply, the barren and inhospitable island of Perim was found unsuitable for troops.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-10) The Sultan of Lahej, Ahmed bin Abdul Karim, then received the detachment for some time at Aden. He proposed to enter into an alliance and to grant Aden as a permanent station, but the offer was declined. A treaty was, however, concluded with the Sultan in 1802 by Admiral Home Popham, who was instructed to enter into political and commercial alliances with the Chiefs of the Arabian coast of the Red Sea.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-:0-11)
texts.4:
### British arrival in Yemen
By the early 1800s, the British were looking for a coaling station to fuel their steamships through their journey from the Suez Canal to the British Raj.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark201029-12) The British tried to negotiate with the Mahra Sultanate to buy the island of Socotra, located in the Arabian Sea, but the Sultan of Mahra refused and told the British naval officer who was tasked with the mission that the island was "the gift of the Almighty to the Mahris".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark201029-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBijl20144-13) In 1835, a year after the British had given up on Socotra, they had attempted to purchase the port city of Aden and its inlet from the Sultan of Lahej, Muhsin Bin Fadl, but they failed. In 1837, the _Duria Dawla_, an Indian ship flying the Union Jack, crashed near the east coast of Aden and was looted by local tribesmen. A year after the incident, in 1838, British officials arrived in Lahej and demanded 12,000 Maria Theresa thalers (MTT) as compensation for the losses. The sultan, unable to pay that sum of money, was forced to cede Aden to the British for a sum of 8,700 MTT a year.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark201031-14) On 19 January 1839, the British East India Company landed Royal Marines at Aden to retain full control of Aden and stop attacks by pirates against British shipping to India.

About this title :
During the early 1960s the Cold War reached its climax. Britain's dwindling power in the Middle East was under siege from Arab nationalism, the Communist bloc and from American designs in the region.
Aden, with its strategic military base and old Protectorate buffer zone, was soon the main battleground.
The 1962 Egyptian-inspired coup in the neighbouring Kingdom of North Yemen further tightened the noose. So began a bitter and bloody insurgency war in South Arabia. British regular an special forces were soon pitted against growing and formidable insurgency forces, fighting both a war in the mountains and an urban conflict in the backstreets of Aden. Intelligence agencies vied for control of 'hearts and minds'.
The British launched a clandestine war in Yemen to keep their enemies at bay. But still the situation in Aden spiralled out of control, culminating in a bloody slaughter in 1967.

The **Aden Emergency**, also known as the **14 October Revolution**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-8) or the **Aden Insurgency**, was an armed rebellion led mainly by the National Liberation Front (NLF) and the Front for the Liberation of Occupied South Yemen (FLOSY) against the British Protectorate and Federation of South Arabia. It began on 14 October 1963 when tribes from Radfan attacked British troops and ended with the proclamation of independence of the [People's Republic of Southern Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_Southern_Yemen "People's Republic of Southern Yemen").

The British had declared a state of emergency following the throwing of a grenade at a gathering of British officials on 10 December 1963 at RAF Khormaksar. A state of emergency was then declared in the British Crown colony of Aden and its hinterland, the Aden Protectorate. The emergency escalated in 1967, which hastened the end of British rule in the territory, which had begun in 1839.

### British arrival in Yemen
[edit]
The first political intercourse between Yemen and the British took place in 1799 during the French invasion of Egypt and Syria, when a naval force was sent from Britain, with a detachment of troops from India, to occupy the island of Perim and prevent all communication of the French in Egypt with the Indian Ocean, by way of the Red Sea. Due to the lack of water supply, the barren and inhospitable island of Perim was found unsuitable for troops.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-10) The Sultan of Lahej, Ahmed bin Abdul Karim, then received the detachment for some time at Aden. He proposed to enter into an alliance and to grant Aden as a permanent station, but the offer was declined. A treaty was, however, concluded with the Sultan in 1802 by Admiral Home Popham, who was instructed to enter into political and commercial alliances with the Chiefs of the Arabian coast of the Red Sea.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-:0-11)

### British arrival in Yemen
By the early 1800s, the British were looking for a coaling station to fuel their steamships through their journey from the Suez Canal to the British Raj.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark201029-12) The British tried to negotiate with the Mahra Sultanate to buy the island of Socotra, located in the Arabian Sea, but the Sultan of Mahra refused and told the British naval officer who was tasked with the mission that the island was "the gift of the Almighty to the Mahris".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark201029-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBijl20144-13) In 1835, a year after the British had given up on Socotra, they had attempted to purchase the port city of Aden and its inlet from the Sultan of Lahej, Muhsin Bin Fadl, but they failed. In 1837, the _Duria Dawla_, an Indian ship flying the Union Jack, crashed near the east coast of Aden and was looted by local tribesmen. A year after the incident, in 1838, British officials arrived in Lahej and demanded 12,000 Maria Theresa thalers (MTT) as compensation for the losses. The sultan, unable to pay that sum of money, was forced to cede Aden to the British for a sum of 8,700 MTT a year.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aden_Emergency#cite_note-FOOTNOTEClark201031-14) On 19 January 1839, the British East India Company landed Royal Marines at Aden to retain full control of Aden and stop attacks by pirates against British shipping to India.

Key facts about the Aden Emergency:
- **Started:** October 14, 1963 (when tribes from Radfan attacked British troops)
- **Ended:** November 30, 1967
- **Result:** British withdrawal and independence of the People's Republic of Southern Yemen

There were later conflicts in the same region as well, including:
- Al-Qaeda insurgency in South Yemen (started 1998)
- Separatist Southern Movement insurgency (started April 27, 2009)

However, the **Aden Emergency of 1963** is the most historically significant insurgency associated with Aden, where the People's Vanguard Party maintained its headquarters.
